items.q: My home was built in the 1980s — how do I know if the roof needs replacing?
items.a: Standard asphalt shingles in the Texas climate typically have a serviceable lifespan of 15–25 years depending on material quality, ventilation, and maintenance history. If your Conroe home is from the 1980s or early 1990s and the roof has never been replaced, it is worth having a professional inspection regardless of whether you see obvious damage. Signs of aging include curling or cupping shingles, widespread granule loss, sagging areas, and frequent minor leaks. Home Team can assess the current condition and tell you honestly whether a targeted repair or full replacement is the better investment.

items.q: How does living near Lake Conroe affect my roof?
items.a: Elevated humidity near Lake Conroe creates conditions where algae and moss growth on shingles is more common than in drier parts of Texas. Moisture retention under debris — pine needles, seed pods, and leaf litter from the area's heavy tree cover — also accelerates shingle breakdown. Proper attic ventilation is especially important in this environment; a poorly ventilated attic traps heat and moisture that degrades shingles from beneath. Home Team evaluates ventilation as part of every inspection in the Conroe area.

items.q: What should I do after a hailstorm in Montgomery County?
items.a: Avoid getting on the roof yourself, particularly after rain. Look at ground-level indicators instead: dented gutters, damaged window screens, granules pooled in downspout outlets, and any obvious missing or cracked shingles visible from the ground. Hail impact is not always immediately visible from the street but can fracture the underlayment and accelerate moisture intrusion. Schedule a professional inspection promptly — storm documentation timing can also matter if you plan to file an insurance claim. Home Team offers free post-storm inspections throughout Conroe and Montgomery County.

items.q: How long does a roof replacement take in Conroe?
items.a: Most residential roof replacements in Conroe are completed in one to two days, depending on roof size, complexity, and the materials selected. Weather is the most common variable — Texas summer storms can interrupt a project, but Home Team monitors conditions and adjusts scheduling accordingly. You will receive a clear timeline before any work begins, and the crew completes a thorough cleanup before each day ends.

topic1.heading: Intense Heat and UV Exposure
topic1.body: Houston-area summers push roof surface temperatures well above the ambient air temperature. Over time, heat and UV radiation break down shingle granules, accelerate asphalt oxidation, and shorten the functional life of an improperly ventilated roof. Quality attic ventilation is not optional in this climate — it is a performance requirement.

topic2.heading: Hail and Severe Storm Seasons
topic2.body: Montgomery County experiences some of the most active severe weather in Texas, including frequent hailstorms that can cause damage not visible from the ground. Bruised shingles, granule loss, and cracked mat layers require close inspection. Even minor hail impact can allow moisture intrusion that worsens significantly over time.

topic3.heading: Tree Canopy and Moisture
topic3.body: Conroe's pine and hardwood tree coverage — particularly near Lake Conroe — means shaded roofs, persistent debris accumulation, and slower drying after rain. These conditions accelerate algae growth and granule wear. Elevated humidity near the lake compounds the effect, making periodic inspections more important than in drier, more open environments.

topic4.heading: Attic Ventilation in Conroe's Climate
topic4.body: Proper attic ventilation is one of the most important and overlooked factors in a roof's longevity. In Conroe's climate — where summer heat is intense and humidity near Lake Conroe is persistent — a poorly ventilated attic traps heat and moisture that degrades shingles from beneath. Adequate soffit intake paired with functional ridge ventilation regulates attic temperature and limits moisture buildup year-round. Home Team evaluates ventilation as a standard part of every inspection in the Conroe area.
